title: Cell-type-specific molecular access throughout the intact adult human brain

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to deliver a functional molecular payload from the bloodstream to a specified cell class across widely separated regions of an intact adult human brain, with sufficiently selective expression and acceptable safety. A payload could encode a sensor or an intervention that changes cellular function. The ambition is distributed access throughout the brain without requiring an injection into each target region. The supplied studies demonstrate relevant delivery components in animal models, but do not demonstrate this combined adult-human capability.

Conceptual synthesis: crossing the blood–brain barrier, entering brain cells, and restricting functional payload expression to the intended cell class are separate requirements. Selective expression would not necessarily mean that only target cells take up the delivery vehicle. Likewise, access to one prespecified class would establish one instance of the capability; a broadly programmable platform would require successful retargeting to additional classes. The title describes the full ambition, while each demonstration would need to state its actual cellular and anatomical coverage.

significance.text: Reliable human delivery would provide a major enabling platform for circuit-directed gene therapy and cell-type sensors. Its immediate consequence would be the ability to equip distributed populations of a chosen cell class with molecular functions that are otherwise difficult to introduce across the adult brain. The technical basis for this possibility includes the CAP-Mac study’s systemic delivery of genetically encoded calcium sensors to newborn macaques and functional sensor responses measured in brain slices. Extending delivery to selected adult-human cell classes would still be a substantial additional achievement.

The supplied Nobel facts page reports that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine recognized discoveries involving light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. This provides context for the importance of molecular tools that influence neural activity, but the award does not establish delivery to a specified cell class throughout an intact adult human brain. The supplied material also does not independently establish the earlier research text’s broader assertion about cell-type-specific optogenetic control in genetically prepared animals.

Conditional synthesis: molecular access could support repair, plasticity interventions, and studies of cognition or memory, but delivery alone would not determine which payload produces a useful effect. Repair would require effective biological mechanisms and disease-specific validation. Cognition and memory applications would require knowledge of the relevant circuits and interventions. Sensor expression would also need a suitable measurement and readout method; equipping cells with sensors does not itself make their signals accessible through an intact human skull. These dependencies limit any analogy between successful delivery and a completed therapy or brain interface.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing combined capability is safe systemic delivery followed by functional expression predominantly in a specified cell class across the adult human brain. The 2023 CAP-Mac paper documents why animal delivery does not automatically supply that capability: few neurotropic adeno-associated virus vectors efficiently cross the blood–brain barrier in non-human primates, and tropism varies with species, developmental stage, and administration route. A capsid effective in one animal context therefore cannot be assumed to retain its distribution or selectivity in adult humans.

Human-receptor targeting addresses an important part of the delivery problem, but receptor-dependent access to the central nervous system is different from selectivity for a chosen brain cell class. The BI-hTFR1 results establish a component based on human transferrin receptor recognition in a human TFRC knockin mouse model. They do not establish the same delivery performance in an adult human, nor do they show that expression can be confined to an arbitrary desired cell class.

Delivery efficiency must also be reconciled with dose and safety. The CAP-Mac paper discusses serious hepatotoxicity and patient deaths reported in the broader high-dose systemic AAV literature. Those reports motivate reducing effective dose and limiting unwanted exposure; they are not evidence that CAP-Mac caused those outcomes. Direct intraparenchymal injections can deliver genes effectively near injection sites, but the paper describes them as impractical for brain-wide transfer. The engineering challenge is therefore distributed delivery with adequate cellular selectivity and a tolerable exposure profile, rather than merely reaching some brain tissue.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing platform would need to maintain useful expression across heterogeneous brain regions, control expression in neighboring cell classes and peripheral tissues, and establish how long the payload remains functional. These requirements must be evaluated together: strong expression in a few locations, broad tissue access without cell-class selectivity, or selective expression at an unacceptable systemic dose would each leave a central part of the proposed capability unresolved.

current_state.text: Chuapoco, Flytzanis, Goeden, and colleagues reported CAP-Mac in Nature Nanotechnology 18, 1241–1251 (2023). The study found neuron-biased tropism in infant Old World primates, broad tropism in adult rhesus macaques, and vasculature-biased tropism in adult marmosets. These are substantial primate delivery results, but their differences show that brain access and cellular distribution depend on species and developmental stage. The paper also reports that AAV-PHP.B does not cross the blood–brain barrier in rhesus macaques, illustrating a limit on transferring vector performance between species.

CAP-Mac also enabled systemic delivery of functional genetically encoded calcium sensors to newborn macaques, with GCaMP responses measured in ex vivo brain slices. This demonstrates functional cargo expression beyond a reporter-only delivery result. Its scope remains newborn macaques and slice-based functional measurement; it does not demonstrate live adult-human sensor readout or selective access to a chosen adult-human cell class. Although the paper discusses serious toxicity associated with high-dose systemic AAV elsewhere, it reports no adverse events or abnormal liver function in its own dosed macaques. That observation should be preserved without treating it as proof of general or long-term human safety.

Huang, Chan, Wu, and colleagues reported BI-hTFR1 in Science 384, 1220–1227, published on 14 June 2024. According to the supplied abstract, the engineered AAV capsid binds human transferrin receptor, crosses human brain endothelial cells, and produces 40–50 times greater central nervous system reporter expression than AAV9 in human TFRC knockin mice. The enhanced tropism was specific to the central nervous system and absent in wild-type mice. The review also records a functional enzyme payload result. Together these findings establish receptor-dependent delivery and functional cargo expression in the model, while central nervous system specificity remains tissue specificity rather than specificity for a selected brain cell class.

The supplied review had the full CAP-Mac article text, methods, and extended-data captions available, but did not independently inspect figure images. For BI-hTFR1, the retained Ovid material consisted of an abstract and editor’s summary despite the full-text form of the supplied URL; full methods and figures were unavailable to that review. The 40–50-fold result is therefore preserved as an abstract-reported comparison, without inferring unreviewed details about dose, sample size, regional uniformity, or experimental variability.

Evidence boundary: the supplied record establishes dated animal-model achievements and their limitations, but contains no freshness search establishing whether subsequent work changed the field by 1 November 2026. It therefore does not establish either completion of the proposed adult-human capability or its continued unresolved status at that date. This gap does not invalidate the reported 2023 and 2024 results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: one systemic administration in adult humans would produce functional payload expression predominantly in a prespecified cell class across distant brain regions, together with a change in a preregistered physiological or clinical measure and acceptable safety. The protocol would define the target class, intended payload function, and expected effect before treatment. These are proposed criteria for convincing evidence, not established regulatory requirements or a claim that such a demonstration has occurred.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurements would include anatomical coverage, the fraction of target cells expressing the payload, expression levels and function, off-target expression in neighboring cell classes and peripheral tissues, expression duration, dose, and safety follow-up. Where feasible, the evidence should distinguish vector distribution and cellular uptake from selective payload expression. Numerical thresholds for useful coverage, selectivity, and acceptable risk would need to be justified for the intended application rather than assumed to be universal.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed measurements would include anatomical coverage, the fraction

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scope and reproducibility requirements: widespread on-target expression in cortex, striatum, and thalamus together would provide an illustrative distributed demonstration, but would not establish coverage throughout the entire brain. Replication across participants and independent studies would be needed to assess reproducibility and variation. Success for one cell class would establish that instance; additional classes, regions, and payloads would need their own evidence before claiming broader programmability. Finite tests establish demonstrated breadth rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed scope and reproducibility requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: broad neuronal expression in a monkey or delivery confined to mice engineered with a human receptor would remain enabling evidence rather than completion of the adult-human goal. A usable platform would also need evidence that its functional effect persists for the intended interval without unacceptable brain or peripheral harm. Demonstrating delivery would not, by itself, establish therapeutic benefit, repair, memory control, or a workable sensor readout system.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NEU-01, simultaneous spike-resolved recording from every neuron in a behaving mammalian brain, could benefit from molecular sensors introduced through a delivery platform. Its defining challenge is comprehensive recording, whereas NEU-09 concerns molecular access to selected classes. NEU-07, noninvasive cellular-resolution read and write through the intact adult human skull, is complementary: NEU-09 could equip cells with sensors or actuators, while NEU-07 would address access to their signals or stimulation through the skull. Neither capability establishes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-02, routine synaptic-resolution connectomics of entire mammalian brains, concerns structural mapping rather than payload delivery. NEU-03, predicting circuit computation from connectivity, concerns explanatory and predictive understanding. Molecular access could support experiments relevant to either, but would not supply a complete connectome or a theory of computation. NEU-04, content-faithful reading and writing of episodic memories, could require targeted molecular interventions, yet additionally requires identifying and manipulating specific memory content with fidelity.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-05, target-specific regrowth of long adult central nervous system axons, and NEU-06, reconstruction of human cognitive circuits after neuronal loss, could use molecular access to deliver repair-related payloads. Their defining breakthroughs remain accurate regrowth and functional circuit reconstruction. NEU-11, reversible and circuit-specific reopening of adult critical-period plasticity, likewise could use targeted delivery, but requires control over the location, timing, and reversibility of plasticity. NEU-09 would enable interventions without establishing these biological outcomes.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-08, a generative developmental code that builds a specified functional circuit, concerns instructions for constructing circuitry rather than access to existing adult cells. NEU-10, a causal, measurement-grade account of conscious content, could draw on targeted perturbation and sensing, but requires a validated causal account beyond delivery. NEU-12, completing sleep’s necessary brain functions without a normal sleep period, might eventually use cell-selective interventions, yet depends on identifying and replacing those functions. These relationships are conditional interpretations of the supplied roster titles; detailed specifications for these concepts were not supplied.

change_log.change: Preserved NEU-09’s identity and whole-brain ambition while separating barrier crossing, cellular uptake, and selective functional expression.
change_log.reason: These are distinct technical requirements; selective expression does not imply exclusive vector uptake.

change_log.change: Replaced blanket claims about inefficient systemic delivery and ineffective direct injections with species-, context-, and coverage-specific descriptions.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence documents limited efficient primate vectors and effective local injections that are impractical for brain-wide transfer.

change_log.change: Integrated CAP-Mac’s species and age differences, functional calcium-sensor results, and the scope of ex vivo measurement.
change_log.reason: These achievements provide important positive evidence while defining the gap to adult-human cell-class access.

change_log.change: Separated broader high-dose systemic AAV toxicity reports from the absence of adverse events or abnormal liver function reported in the CAP-Mac macaques.
change_log.reason: The earlier wording risked attributing external toxicity outcomes to CAP-Mac.

change_log.change: Preserved the BI-hTFR1 40–50-fold comparison, identified AAV9 as the comparator, and added receptor dependence and functional cargo findings.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supports these results while limiting them to the reported model and abstract-level evidence.

change_log.change: Retained the supplied Nobel statement while qualifying the broader animal optogenetics assertion.
change_log.reason: The prize page supports recognition of optogenetics, but does not substantiate the earlier claim’s full scientific scope.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to specify coverage, selectivity, duration, function, safety, and reproducibility without inventing numerical standards.
change_log.reason: A distributed three-region demonstration or success for one class cannot establish whole-brain coverage or arbitrary class targeting.

change_log.change: Integrated explicit dependencies for therapies, repair, cognition, memory, and sensor readout.
change_log.reason: Molecular access is an enabling platform rather than evidence that downstream applications have been solved.

change_log.change: Explained relationships with all other supplied roster entries using conditional, title-based synthesis.
change_log.reason: The roster supports useful distinctions, although full concept definitions remain unavailable.

change_log.change: Preserved review access limitations and separated dated findings from unassessed November 2026 freshness.
change_log.reason: Available evidence supports the historical results without establishing the latest field-wide position.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish whether later research achieved or materially changed the proposed capability by 1 November 2026.
The BI-hTFR1 full methods and figures were unavailable to the supplied review, leaving detailed assessment of the reported effect size and experimental boundaries incomplete.
Application-specific numerical requirements for coverage, target-cell expression, off-target expression, duration, dose, and safety remain to be justified.
The record does not establish adult-human delivery performance, repeatable targeting across multiple cell classes, or comprehensive anatomical coverage.
The broader assertion about cell-type-specific optogenetic control in genetically prepared animals remains unsubstantiated by the supplied texts; it is qualified rather than treated as false.
Relationships to other NEU concepts are inferred from supplied titles; detailed specifications would be needed to verify their precise dependencies.
